system.name: Orq
system.one_liner: a system for collaborative analytics on private data using secure multiparty computation that eliminates the quadratic cost of secure joins

content.subject: how three parties jointly compute a secure AND using shares and one round of z-value communication

elements.name: Secret Sharing
elements.role: defines x and y as XOR-shared across 3 parties (x = x1 xor x2 xor x3), with a worked example (6 = 15 xor 8 xor 1)

elements.name: Random Sharing of Zero
elements.role: defines a 3-way sharing of 0 (0 = r1 xor r2 xor r3) used to re-randomize the AND result, with a worked example (0 = 17 xor 63 xor 46)

elements.name: Functionality
elements.role: states the goal z = x AND y and its worked check (4 = 6 AND 13 = 31 xor 63 xor 36)

elements.name: P1
elements.role: first party; holds two of the three shares of x and y, computes 'local' and z1

elements.name: P2
elements.role: second party; computes 'local' and z2 from its shares

elements.name: P3
elements.role: third party; computes 'local' and z3 from its shares

elements.name: local
elements.role: each party's AND cross-term over its two known shares of x and y, computed before masking

elements.name: z1
elements.role: P1's local term masked with random share r1; sent on to P2

elements.name: z2
elements.role: P2's local term masked with random share r2; sent on to P3

elements.name: z3
elements.role: P3's local term masked with random share r3; sent on to P1

relations.what: P1 sends its masked result z1 to P2
P2 sends its masked result z2 to P3
P3 sends its masked result z3 to P1

steps.what: P1 computes local := x1y1 xor x1y2 xor x2y1 = 14, then z1 := local xor r1 = 31
P2 computes local := x2y2 xor x2y3 xor x3y2 = 0, then z2 := local xor r2 = 63
P3 computes local := x3y3 xor x3y1 xor x1y3 = 10, then z3 := local xor r3 = 36
P1 sends its masked result to P2
P2 sends its masked result to P3
P3 sends its masked result to P1

values.what: concrete numeric shares and results for one worked AND instance: x=6 shared as (15,8,1), y=13 shared as (72,14,75), zero shared as 0=(17,63,46), giving z=4=6 AND 13 reconstructed as 31 xor 63 xor 36

content.key_idea: Three parties can jointly compute a boolean AND on XOR-secret-shared inputs by each locally combining its two known share-pairs, masking the result with a pre-shared zero, and sending that single masked value once around a ring.
content.reading_order: top to bottom through the Initialization definitions and worked numbers, then left to right through the three parties' Local Computation boxes, then around the Communication ring

evidence: Figure 3 and the example below discuss the AND protocol for our replicated three-party
So-called replicated secret-sharing protocols distribute multiple shares to each party
Parties perform local computation on their shares

summary: Figure 3 walks through Araki et al.'s secure AND protocol for Orq's replicated three-party (semi-honest, honest-majority) MPC, using one concrete numeric example. Initialization defines XOR secret sharing (x=6 as 15,8,1; y=13 as 72,14,75) and a pre-agreed sharing of zero (0=17,63,46), with the target z=x AND y=4 shown reconstructing as 31 xor 63 xor 36. Step 1 Local Computation shows each party Pi, holding two of the three shares of x and y, computing a local AND cross-term (14, 0, and 10 respectively) and masking it with its share of zero to get zi (31, 63, 36). Step 2 Communication then sends each zi once around a ring, P1 to P2 to P3 to P1, so every party ends up with a full additive share of z without ever learning x, y, or z directly.
summary_zh: 该图用具体数值演示Orq三方MPC安全AND协议：初始化定义x、y的异或分享及零分享；步骤①各方用两份分享做本地AND并用零分享掩盖得zi；步骤②各方将zi沿P1→P2→P3→P1环发送一轮，重构出z=x∧y而不泄露原值。
